I've been wanting to build a new AR for a while and decided I was going to get an 80% lower. Well, one thing led to another and I ended up buying an 80% lower from polymer80...

Anyone have any experience with these here? I've yet to actually mill it out. The fit for the magazine and upper from my other AR was solid and the lower seems made well enough.
What is your experience with polymer AR lowers?

I've broken them. If you are doing an 80% just get billet, it is like sculpting butter anyway since it is aluminum.

TN Armsco is popular because they are re-enforced. I don't know that they are offering 80% but you can buy a two pack for less than $100. I've shot a redditor's build on one and it felt fine.

The only reason I got a poly 80% lower was for playing around with. It'll be used for an AR pistol. I've seen some break in the past but it appears to be always where the buffer tube connects. I am uncertain if this is a result of people picking it up by the buffer tube and putting a lot of pressure/weight on that area or what. I figured a light-weight AR pistol build would minimize that.

It's a point of mechanic stress. That is where all the mechanical action happens. The buffer is putting the spring tension on the bolt and the bolt is the piston. That means all the energy ultimately pulls on the back of the receiver where the buffer tube screws in.
I've looked over the TN Armsco stuff and if I want to build another AR pistol may go that route as well.
Please let us know how it goes. Maybe keep a logbook on it so you have a round count if it breaks.

TN Arms polymer lowers are just as good as an aluminum lower. I've got a couple of them, they're light, they're cheap, and they're (figuratively) bulletproof. If you want to mill out an 80% lower then get aluminum, an 80% polymer kind of defeats the purpose.

Every polymer lower on the market, the sole exception that I've seen being TN Arms, will break. I don't even mean "they'll break eventually," I mean they'll break almost immediately with moderate use. They're completely worthless garbage and frankly I don't know how they still sell them or why someone hasn't gotten sued for selling them yet because everyone, including the manufacturer, knows they're going to break by now. If you're going to get one, get one from TN Arms.

Cav Arms polymer lowers are the best. They are now made by GWACS Armory. They are 1-piece lowers with a fixed stock and grip. That is also the disadvantage: lack of customization. The stock length is slightly smaller than M16A1 stock length. They are light and durable and there are torture tests of them on Youtube.
Buy 2 of them. That way you don't have to wait when the first one breaks.
I almost bought some cheap $50 ones last December. But then Anderson started selling theirs for $40. So I bought 5. Christmas shopping was easy.

I got 3 polymers for a AR pistol build, but the 80 percenters were out of spec so I'm going to have to either re-mill them or give up on them and make a metal lower.

http://www.eparmory.com/ did not deliver a quality product. Two were "blemished" lowers that were supposed to be fully to spec just some cosmetic issues and it ended up being out of spec by far. The other was a retail lower and it too was out of spec. If you do get them find a jig because the "hole drill guides" are way off. I'm done with polymer until I can find another company that's affordable enough and not have air bubbles in the plastic that weaken the structure.

I realized this on the drive home last night:

  • My Steam library has 106 games.
  • A few of those are pack-ins that I didn’t want and won’t ever play, like GTA 1~3. So let’s call it 95 games.
  • I’ve logged at least 8 hours in 20 games. (or “enough hours” if they’re shorter than 8 like Portal)
  • I’ve beaten/completed 11 games.

It’s not possible to estimate how long it would take to beat/complete the remaining games, but if we establish 8 hours as the minimum to really play a game, then I have 75 * 8 = 600 hours of accrued playtime debt. If all I did EVERY DAY was play, for 8 hours a day, that’s almost 3 months. But obviously for me that’s completely impossible because I have job-wife-kid-other-fucking-hobbies.

What’s even more scary, is that if I only played 1 hour per day it would still take almost TWO YEARS, and I can also confirm that I could never find time to play one hour per day in my life as it is today.

And this isn’t taking into account games that you’d want to play for MORE than 8 hours, like Fallout or Scrolls…
